title: Ruling on Business Return Timing — Northgate Purchases & Returns Business Restocking
content:
This ruling fixes how the timing of a return affects the business restocking charge that Northgate Purchases & Returns invoices on a changed-mind return of special-order merchandise for a Northgate Business Membership or Northgate Business Plus Membership.

## Ruling

Business return timing: when the return authorization was requested no more than 14 calendar days after the purchase's fulfillment date, the business restocking charge is taken at 0.6 of its amount; when it was requested 15 to 21 calendar days after, at 0.8 of its amount; otherwise at its full amount (1). Days are counted as calendar days, the fulfillment date being day 0.

The request date is the requested date recorded on the return authorization the member is confirming; the fulfillment date is the one recorded on the purchase. The multiplier applies to the amount that the business restocking rate yields on the returned value, before that amount is rounded half up to the cent.

| Days from the fulfillment date to the request | Share of the charge taken |
|---|---|
| 0 to 14 | 0.6 |
| 15 to 21 | 0.8 |
| 22 or more | 1 (full amount) |

## Calendar boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Fulfillment date (day 0) | Authorization requested | Day count | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 May | 15 May | 14 | 0.6 |
| 1 May | 16 May | 15 | 0.8 |
| 1 May | 22 May | 21 | 0.8 |
| 1 May | 23 May | 22 | 1 |

## Worked multiplier (hypothetical amount)

A percentage amount of 211.20 requested on day 10 is taken at 0.6: 126.72. The same amount requested on day 18 is taken at 0.8: 168.96. A percentage amount of 100.01 on day 10 gives 60.006, rounded half up to 60.01.
